shoal_e03_entry.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_entry.text: Day Two Hundred Thirty-Two began with a smell of wet rope and onions frying somewhere beyond the yard wall. Yue signed the bounded restoration post beside its qualified supervisor and wage receiver. Thirty five-copper shifts across six weeks, beginning today, bought specified work on forty unloaded housings. It did not buy her nights, a cure for her shoulder, or a miraculous answer when an ordinary part was beyond repair. Then she put the page away and picked up the broom assigned for the first hour.

shoal_e03_work_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_work_01.text: The broom had a shortened handle, polished smooth by someone whose hand rested lower than Yue's. She tried to work at that height and felt the wrong pull across her back. The supervisor fetched a handle that fit rather than telling her to endure it. Beside her, a veteran sorter watched with the expression of someone who had asked for the same change last month. He wanted to know whether a cultivator's discomfort had finally made ordinary handles worth buying.

shoal_e03_work_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_work_02.text: Yue stopped sweeping. She could explain her cleared shoulder, but that would not answer his question. The supervisor checked the tool issue list and found two earlier handle requests still awaiting action. Both would be filled from the same materials allowance if the current batch genuinely needed them. The sorter tested the longer handle first. He did not thank Yue for arriving. She liked him for refusing a gratitude that would have hidden whose request had come before hers.

shoal_e03_work_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_work_03.text: They cleared the comparison lane without moving owner-marked parts. Sand had worked under the lowest stack during the recent wet weather. Yue pushed it into a pan while the sorter showed her how to leave a visible gap around every blocked fuel socket. A tidy sweep that erased the gap would look better and inspect worse. The work stained her sleeve almost immediately. She found the loss of her road-clean appearance oddly relieving, as though she had finally stopped arriving.

shoal_e03_work_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_work_04.text: Han entered the first shift's actual hours only after the morning task began. Each accepted shift paid five copper; the wage receiver would issue six weekly settlements of twenty-five copper for five performed shifts, totaling one hundred fifty when complete. Any unperformed day needed its own later agreement rather than a fictitious mark. Yue chose the posted room rate from her own wages and savings. No one had promised that the proposed labor payment included permanent housing.

shoal_e03_work_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_work_05.text: The forty housings varied more than the draft drawing suggested. Some had wide lips polished by hands, some thin stamped rims that cut cloth, some owner repairs using soft metal where an earlier maker had used hardwood. Yue sorted them only under the supervisor's categories. She did not infer function from a beautiful shape. One casing carried a painted bird whose tail covered an old seam. Its owner had painted it for a child, and the seam still needed examination.

shoal_e03_work_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_work_06.text: A rigger named only on the ordinary work roster asked whether the bird should be washed off. The supervisor said the comparison did not require it today. Removing someone's decoration because it made an object easier to describe would destroy something beyond the funded scope. Yue drew a small exterior outline with the owner's permitted mark instead. The bird made the casing memorable. It did not make the casing safe, enchanted, or more deserving of return than the plain ones.

shoal_e03_work_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_work_07.text: By midmorning, her shoulder began to feel hot in the old familiar strip. She reported it before trying another lift. The supervisor reassigned her to seated tag preparation within the accepted restricted tasks and kept the parts out of reach. She wanted to protest that the sensation was mild. A mild warning was the point at which a stop cost least. The veteran sorter brought the needed tags over and resumed his own lifting without making her recovery into a public lesson.

shoal_e03_work_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_work_08.text: On the seat, Yue could hear how the yard worked when she was not trying to prove she belonged in it. A porter cursed an empty barrel for rolling in the wrong direction. Someone called back that emptiness had never improved a merchant. The supervisor laughed once and then told them to wedge the barrel. It was an ordinary unsafe object with an ordinary remedy. The joke did not need a cultivation comparison, which made it funnier to Yue.

shoal_e03_work_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_work_09.text: After the restricted hour, the supervisor ended her technical work for that shift. She had performed paid ordinary duties, and the allowed reassignment was documented under the existing terms. Qualified care would assess persistent symptoms if they continued; the forty-copper reserve did not require her to become more injured before it could be used. Yue took the prescribed rest interval without qi self-treatment. Her earned sixth stage remained earned. It could not buy yesterday's shoulder back.

shoal_e03_work_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_work_10.text: She walked to the public lane after work while the rest of the yard continued. A fisherman mended a net around a gap large enough for the fish he claimed were never there. He asked if she could fix the tear with energy. Yue said she could hold a loose end while he tied it, if that was useful and within her cleared range. He gave her the end. The short task produced an actual knot rather than a discussion of the power she lacked.

shoal_e03_work_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_work_11.text: On the next morning, the shoulder's warning heat had settled with ordinary rest, but Yue's grip check still belonged to the qualified work review. The supervisor compared her current motion and reported symptoms with her previous clearance. He allowed the planned seated unloaded observation, not heavy handling. She had slept reasonably and eaten enough. The ordinary conditions mattered. A difficult emotion alone did not diagnose injury, and a hopeful emotion did not certify recovery.

shoal_e03_work_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_work_12.text: The observation bench depended on the permissions Yue actually brought from Lark. The common method could be used at an open table under its offered scope. A licensed private kit needed its declared supplier room and dates. A completed independent dispatch gave no instrument rights at all. The supervisor would not merge these situations merely because the operator was the same woman. Today's accepted salvage employment paid today's work. It did not purchase whatever an old source had withheld.

shoal_e03_work_13.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_work_13.text: Before they set up, a port worker carried in a damaged crate lid from the shallow-water yard. It had been part of a mixed storage stack caught by a recent tide. The storage owner now consented to retrieve two identified small crates when ordinary crews could reach them. One contained handcut printing blocks intended for a public school gift. The other contained old clinic-owned glass sleeves for unpowered lamps. Their location had deteriorated while licensed crews finished safer priorities.

shoal_e03_work_14.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_work_14.text: The public school had not yet accepted the gift. Its maker's daughter still owned the printing blocks and wanted to decide after seeing their condition. The clinic already owned its sleeves and had agreed to ordinary retrieval if feasible. Neither crate held a person, a secret cultivation weapon, or evidence that would justify endangering a crew. They were objects with real uses and owners. The tide forecast gave their retrieval a finite morning window before the exposed stack shifted again.

shoal_e03_work_15.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_work_15.text: Yan inspected the route personally. The damaged storage surface would allow one light crate to cross under a supervised ordinary lift before the crew withdrew. A second trip would overlap a scheduled crane movement and the rising water. He refused the storage owner's request to treat an extra quarter-hour as a kindness. The route's danger did not become smaller because both contents were worthwhile. His crew had a paid duty to leave before the crane movement, and he intended to honor it.

shoal_e03_work_16.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_work_16.text: The supervisor asked Yue whether the funded batch could include sorting the retrieved parts at ordinary waist height. The clinic sleeves fitted the approved housing comparison scope. The printing blocks did not, but a separately offered school-side paid half-day could employ another worker to handle them; Yue would provide only her off-shift chosen assistance within safe limits. He would not charge the restoration account for an attractive side project. Yan's retrieval itself remained paid by the storage account.

shoal_e03_work_17.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_work_17.text: Yue disliked how readily one worthwhile object fitted a wage column and another required more people to say yes. The maker's daughter did not. She wanted the blocks retrieved by someone who remembered they were still hers, not absorbed into a public grant because her father had meant to give them away. She could accept an ordinary delayed gift or decline it altogether. The blocks' future was a family decision even if their immediate retrieval used a licensed crew.

shoal_e03_work_18.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_work_18.text: The clinic keeper explained that the sleeves were replacement parts, not medicine. Losing them would require a paid later order and postpone the particular lamp maintenance session that used them. Patients would still receive available ordinary care, under the clinic's existing lighting arrangements and limits. Saving glass could matter without becoming a promise to heal anyone. Yue listened to the concrete inconvenience instead of inventing a life-or-death story to make the choice obvious.

shoal_e03_work_19.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_work_19.text: The printing blocks contained an alphabet, tide illustrations, and a long comic row of fish with human hats. The maker's daughter remembered her father's mistakes in the fish more vividly than his careful letters. He had died years before, unrelated to the burned lamp store. Some blocks could be copied if recovered; if lost before a copy, they would remain lost. Yue would not recover their exact surfaces by remembering a description or sensing the intention of a dead craftsman.

shoal_e03_work_20.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_work_20.text: At lunch, the yard sorter said clinics always won because their needs sounded official. A rigger replied that children also needed light to learn. He Ming asked whether either of them had asked the owners what they wanted instead of turning the crates into a contest between occupations. The daughter wanted the offered retrieval and retained the right to refuse the school gift. The clinic keeper wanted the permitted parts. Their requests were still incompatible within Yan's safe window.

shoal_e03_work_21.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_work_21.text: The ordinary port priorities had already assigned larger crews to a damaged passenger landing and two occupied boats. Neither assignment would be canceled to make this choice disappear. No passenger was left waiting on a dangerous landing while Yue chose between glass and wood. She could decide which small retrieval she would support under the offered terms, then bear the loss of the other. It was a modest power, uncomfortable because nobody could pretend it was enough.

shoal_e03_work_22.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_work_22.text: She inspected the crate labels from the safe observation point. The ink matched the owners' descriptions, and the visible crate weights were within the planned ordinary lift. Yue did not walk onto the failing storage surface or test it with qi. Yan described the withdrawal signal and the place where all observers would wait. When the crane's preparatory bell sounded, the retrieval would end whether or not the chosen crate had moved. The bell belonged to the crane operator, not to Yue's preference.

shoal_e03_work_23.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_work_23.text: The maker's daughter offered to accompany the recovered blocks to the sorting room if that crate was chosen. The clinic keeper would receive the sleeves at its ordinary parts desk under the alternative. Their actual attendance made each future tangible. Yue could imagine the daughter opening a fish block and the keeper fitting a sound sleeve. She could also imagine both disappointed faces. Wanting to spare everyone disappointment was not a plan that Yan's crew could execute.

shoal_e03_work_24.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_work_24.text: Rong asked whether the retrieval could be bought faster. Yan said another qualified crew could not appear inside the remaining window, whatever its hypothetical fee. The merchant accepted that answer more quickly than Yue had. He was used to missing a tide even after paying for a booking. He offered no hidden rescue and claimed no right to own what survived. For once, his impatience simply brought the practical limit into sharper focus.

shoal_e03_work_25.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_work_25.text: Before making the selection, Yue told the supervisor she would keep the new technical shift inside its assigned batch and use only permitted ordinary assistance for the selected retrieval. He confirmed that she would not be on the unstable storage surface. Her cultivation would play no part in the lift. The choice belonged to which recoverable material she supported and later worked with. A certificate could make others ask her to do more; it could not make the offered window longer.

shoal_e03_work_26.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_work_26.text: Yan's crew checked the landing rope and prepared the single empty handcart. The daughter stood near the school clerk; the clinic keeper held a receiving cloth. Both owners had consented to their own possible retrieval, and neither would be asked to surrender title as a condition of help. Yue looked at the two receiving places. The morning would leave one occupied and the other empty. She had to choose before the safe route closed, not after seeing which ending hurt less.

shoal_e03_retrieval_choice.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_retrieval_choice.text: The ordinary crew could retrieve one light crate within the inspected window. The printing blocks preserved a dead maker's unrepeated work, with their living owner still deciding whether to give them to the school. The clinic sleeves could support a specific maintenance session, avoiding a replacement order and delay. People and occupied boats already had the larger crews. Yue chose which permitted material retrieval she would support.

choices.text: Support retrieval of the printing blocks and their owner's later decision.
Support retrieval of the clinic's glass sleeves for the scheduled maintenance.

shoal_e03_blocks_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_blocks_01.text: The daughter brought her own cloth to the receiving point and agreed that damaged blocks should remain identifiable before anyone tried to scrub them. Yue told the clinic keeper the other crate would not be retrieved in this window. He accepted the operational decision without calling it harmless. The maintenance session would need a later order and revised date. He took his receiving cloth back to the clinic. His departure left a space that the chosen object's value could not fill.

shoal_e03_blocks_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_blocks_02.text: Yan's crew worked without Yue inside its lift boundary. One hand walked the stable approach, another controlled the prepared line, and the cart keeper stayed on the inspected landing. The first crate handle broke when the line took its permitted ordinary strain. Yan stopped the lift before anyone reached for the slipping wood. They reset the sling around the crate's base. The short delay consumed time but did not change the crane operator's scheduled bell.

shoal_e03_blocks_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_blocks_03.text: The daughter gripped her folded cloth hard enough to whiten a knuckle. Yue stood beside her and said nothing about her father's intention guiding the lift. The only intention moving the crate belonged to living workers using inspected equipment. When the sling held, the crate crossed the stable edge and settled onto the handcart. Yan checked the load before allowing the observers near it. Yue could finally see a split in the lid where water had entered.

shoal_e03_blocks_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_blocks_04.text: The crane's preparatory bell sounded while the crew withdrew its line. Yan called the retrieval closed. No one used the success to argue for the second trip. They rolled the chosen crate away from the landing and returned the access rope to its owner. The clinic keeper was already gone. Yue heard the crew's ordinary jokes start again after the rope was secure. Their relief did not mean the lost crate had become unimportant.

shoal_e03_blocks_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_blocks_05.text: At the permitted sorting table, the daughter opened the crate herself. The upper blocks were soaked but recognizable. Lower down, wood had swollen against wood until two surfaces tore when separated. She stopped before doing more damage and asked the school-side worker to find a conservation reader who could advise on ordinary drying. Yue held the open lid at waist height. She did not warm the blocks with qi or claim that subtle circulation would restore their cut faces.

shoal_e03_blocks_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_blocks_06.text: The separately offered school half-day paid its accepted worker from the school's current preparation account, outside Yue's restoration appropriation. Yue's own assistance remained off-shift and ordinary. It ended when her shoulder began to tire. The daughter thanked her for saying so and found another prop for the lid. The rescued crate did not become a reason to turn every person near it into unpaid help until its owner was satisfied.

shoal_e03_blocks_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_blocks_07.text: They counted twelve blocks with readable faces, three needing ordinary specialist assessment, and five damaged beyond their present identification. One of the readable blocks showed a fish wearing a hat too tall for its head. The daughter laughed, then cried with the laugh still in her throat. Her father had carved that fish while angry about a tax official. Yue had not known him. She could stand beside the memory without pretending that retrieving wood made it hers.

shoal_e03_blocks_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_blocks_08.text: The daughter allowed the school clerk to photograph the readable faces by ordinary permitted copying once they were dry. She withheld the family dedication until she had spoken with her brother. The school accepted no gift today. Yue wrote the offered copying scope and left the unoffered material blank. The actual room was full of wet wood, not a symbolic triumph of public access. Permission could grow later through the owner's decision, or remain where it was.

shoal_e03_blocks_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_blocks_09.text: From the yard fence, they heard a sharper cracking sound from the exposed storage stack. The crane's crew had stopped its own movement and cleared the zone as the tide lifted a weakened support. Through the public observation gap, Yue saw the clinic crate break against a piling and its contents scatter into inaccessible moving water. Yan recorded that visible loss without sending a hand after it. A second heroic attempt would have endangered the people who had just completed the safe first one.

shoal_e03_blocks_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_blocks_10.text: The clinic keeper returned after receiving the report. He could verify the lost crate's identity by its visible outer mark before the dispersal, but he could not count each broken sleeve from the lane. He canceled the planned sleeve-maintenance session and filed a replacement request under the clinic's own account. Available ordinary care continued under existing limits. Yue listened while he named the delayed work. She did not defend the blocks by making the clinic's loss sound smaller.

shoal_e03_blocks_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_blocks_11.text: That evening, the daughter placed the readable blocks on a permitted drying rack and locked the unassessed pieces in her own labeled box. Yue had no key. The school clerk wanted to announce that the gift was saved; the daughter corrected him. Some surfaces were saved, some were lost, and the gift was not yet accepted. The correction disappointed a neat public story. It gave the living owner room to decide what a partial inheritance should become.

shoal_e03_blocks_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_blocks_12.text: Song Mei came to the drying room by the daughter's invitation, carrying no instrument. She recognized the absurd hat fish and offered to ask a printmaker about ordinary drying, subject to the daughter's consent. She did not promise to build a performance around the rescue. Yue watched two artists discuss grain, ink, and an old man's bad jokes. Their conversation had a precision she rarely heard when people described art as something that simply cheered a community.

shoal_e03_blocks_13.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_blocks_13.text: On the next day, the printmaker advised slow ordinary drying and rejected a quick heated frame that might split the blocks further. The owner paid the bounded assessment fee from her own offered repair purse and retained the remaining decision. Yue returned to her restoration shift. Her chosen retrieval had created a living work sequence she could visit if invited. It had also created a postponed clinic session that she could not recover by working harder in the school room.

shoal_e03_blocks_14.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_blocks_14.text: Before the fifth accepted shift ended, Han paid Yue the first twenty-five copper against the five performed days. The school work was absent from that wage count. Yue kept her paid labor and chosen ordinary assistance separate, not because the latter had no value but because it belonged to people who might refuse her next invitation. In her private note, she named the survived surfaces and the lost maintenance date. Both had begun with the same tide window.

shoal_e03_glass_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_glass_01.text: The clinic keeper spread his receiving cloth on the permitted cart surface and showed the crew the crate's current ownership mark. Yue told the maker's daughter that the printing blocks would not be retrieved in this window. The daughter nodded once and turned away before she could be asked to admire the clinic's usefulness. She still owned what would be lost. Yue let her leave without trying to extract a gracious sentence for the story of the chosen rescue.

shoal_e03_glass_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_glass_02.text: Yan's crew entered through the stable approach with the inspected ordinary sling. Yue remained beyond the observer rope. A crate handle broke under the first permitted strain, and Yan stopped the movement before a worker tried to catch the wood. They reset the sling around the base. The clinic keeper asked whether the delay changed the withdrawal time. It did not. The crane operator's preparatory bell would still end this retrieval, even if the crate had not crossed.

shoal_e03_glass_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_glass_03.text: The sling held on the second setup. The crate moved slowly enough that Yue could see water leaking through its lower seam. She wanted to tell the crew which side looked weaker, but Yan had already assigned a worker with the better angle. She stayed quiet unless asked for an observation. Too many helpful voices could blur the command that mattered. When the crate settled onto the handcart, the keeper exhaled and checked the receiving mark before approaching.

shoal_e03_glass_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_glass_04.text: The bell sounded while the crew withdrew the line. Yan closed the access window and returned the approach rope to its assigned position. Success gave nobody a new trip. The crate of printing blocks remained on the exposed stack, its owner absent from the receiving point. Yue rolled the permitted cart only after Yan said the landing route was clear. Her part used ordinary hands at waist height. Six primary pairs made no difference to the crate's weight.

shoal_e03_glass_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_glass_05.text: The clinic parts desk was cooler than the yard, with a shaded shelf and a cloth over the clean table. The keeper opened the crate himself. Two top sleeves were cracked, and more glass rattled below. Yue helped lift intact parts onto his receiving cloth within the permitted restoration sorting scope. She wore ordinary hand protection. No qi passed into the glass. A warm or bright response would not tell the clinic whether a sleeve was sound enough to fit safely.

shoal_e03_glass_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_glass_06.text: A qualified clinic maintenance worker examined each surviving sleeve against the existing ordinary lamp specifications. Twelve fitted within the stated tolerances. Four were cracked, and two required a separate decision because an earlier repair had changed their rims. The keeper retained title to all of them, including rejected pieces. Yue's observation did not authorize a fueled application. He marked the fit result as unloaded and scheduled the clinic's own qualified maintenance session for its actual available date.

shoal_e03_glass_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_glass_07.text: One rejected sleeve carried a scratched flower near its rim. The keeper said a former attendant had marked personal working equipment that way, before the clinic acquired the parts properly. Yue asked whether he wanted the mark retained in the return description. He did. Even a clinical object could carry a person's memory without becoming sacred or safe. The glass was no less dangerous when cracked because someone had once cared enough to scratch a flower into it.

shoal_e03_glass_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_glass_08.text: Outside the parts desk, a patient asked whether the rescued glass meant the clinic would reopen late appointments immediately. The keeper said it supported one scheduled maintenance session; fuel, qualified staffing, and posted clinical hours still governed appointments. The patient was disappointed and asked for the current ordinary desk. Yue directed her there without supplying a brighter promise. A rescued component could matter and still fail to provide the thing a waiting person most wanted today.

shoal_e03_glass_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_glass_09.text: The exposed storage stack cracked as the tide lifted its weakened support. The crane crew stopped its own scheduled movement and cleared the zone. From the public observation gap, Yue saw the marked printing crate strike a piling, open, and release dark wooden pieces into inaccessible moving water. Yan recorded the observed dispersal without sending anyone into it. The exact cut faces had never been copied. The safe first retrieval did not create a safe second one after the loss.

shoal_e03_glass_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_glass_10.text: The maker's daughter returned to hear the report in person. She identified the crate mark from Yan's recorded observation and chose not to visit the wet edge herself. No one could inventory each scattered block from the public lane. She declined the school clerk's offer to commission imagined replacements with her father's name on them. New art might come later. It would not be the lost original surfaces, and she would decide whether the family wanted it.

shoal_e03_glass_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_glass_11.text: Song Mei met the daughter outside the partnership room and asked whether she wanted company walking home. The daughter accepted the walk and declined a public lament. Yue saw them turn into the ordinary lane together. Their absence was a consequence of her chosen access window, not a relationship penalty measured against her. People could find comfort away from the person whose decision had preceded a loss. Yue did not follow them to make sure she was forgiven.

shoal_e03_glass_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_glass_12.text: The clinic completed the permitted twelve-sleeve unloaded fit check on its scheduled afternoon. Its maintenance worker rejected the two altered rims and set the cracked pieces in a closed owner-marked waste container pending proper disposal. Yue signed only her actual sorting hours within the restoration post. The clinic's work did not consume the school-side fee that would have applied to the other retrieval. An unused alternative payment remained unused rather than becoming an invisible reward for efficiency.

shoal_e03_glass_13.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_glass_13.text: At the end of the first five accepted shifts, Han paid Yue twenty-five copper against the actual performed days. She had helped preserve replacement parts for a bounded maintenance session. She had also watched an unrepeated maker's work disperse. The wage did not measure the moral balance between those outcomes. Yue put it in her own purse and kept the retrieval record beside the clinic's changed appointment, where neither could quietly replace the other.

shoal_e03_glass_14.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_glass_14.text: That evening, she passed a shop window containing an ordinary printed fish in a plain hat. The resemblance hurt because it was slight. Anyone could make another comic fish. No one could honestly claim that the lost blocks had returned through a convenient new drawing. Yue bought nothing from the window and walked on. The clinic keeper's gratitude had been sincere, and the daughter's loss remained real. A decision could be defensible without becoming clean.

shoal_e03_lark_gate.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_lark_gate.text: The first ordinary shifts left the restoration batch ready for its source-specific unloaded comparison. The supervisor checked the current method permission and the tools actually available to Yue before setting the work area. The chosen retrieval had not changed either permission. She would perform the next task within the terms she had brought, using the separate port employment she had now accepted.

shoal_e03_public_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_public_01.text: The open table used the consented public comparison pages. Port-owned ordinary rulers and a borrowed school straightedge supported exterior unloaded observations; no Lark contact board or private freight-signal appendix appeared. Two packers could watch under the public table's current capacity rule. One noticed that the housing's bird mark had been drawn upside down. Yue corrected her outline before comparing the actual seam. A public method could benefit from an ordinary owner who knew an object by touch.

shoal_e03_public_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_public_02.text: The supervisor limited the task to permitted visible dimensions and separately blocked fuel sockets. Yue could record where the public method gave no answer. A private freight-signal tolerance was among those unanswered questions. Rong would have preferred a definitive fit result for his supplier order. The public table could not honestly provide it today. Yue left that part pending instead of converting broad access into expertise that its offered pages did not contain.

shoal_e03_public_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_public_03.text: The packers contributed a current handling observation with their own permission: one rim snagged a sleeve when carried from the left. They declined to have their names printed beside it. Yue recorded the anonymous handling direction and the date. The observation did not decide a hidden technical defect, but it changed where the supervisor placed hand protection for ordinary returns. People outside the private bench could improve the work without being treated as replacement examiners.

shoal_e03_public_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_public_04.text: At the end of the session, the school straightedge returned to its lender with a current condition receipt. The port rulers stayed with the port. Yue retained only the permitted public observations and the source pages under their declared scope. No exclusive equipment loan had materialized from the open method. Her ordinary wage paid a useful limited shift. It did not buy the missing private answer or make the unchosen supplier room unnecessary to every future task.

shoal_e03_public_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_public_05.text: Rong accepted the pending fit result and revised the delivery list around what had actually been checked. The two packers took the public handling note back to their own group. Yue could hear their argument about which sleeve had snagged first as they left. Broad participation gave her more ordinary angles, not unanimity. The port batch now carried an explicit limit that a customer would have to read before treating a marked housing as qualified for a fueled application.

shoal_e03_private_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_private_01.text: After the required port clearance, the supervisor opened the Lark-owned kit in the inspected supplier bench room. He checked the zero-load contact board, external copper comparison strip, and waxed stop cover against the incoming inventory. No fuel or stones had arrived with them. The private appendix covered freight-signal geometry, not Yue's bodily routes. Current use fell inside Days Two Hundred Fifteen through Two Hundred Sixty-Five, and the carrier return deadline remained unchanged.

shoal_e03_private_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_private_02.text: The room allowed a particular unloaded geometry comparison that the open public pages did not supply. Yue worked beside the qualified supervisor, with the stop cover in its assigned position and no energy applied. Rong could receive the permitted supplier result without copying the private appendix into a public packet. The two packers who had asked to attend were not inside this licensed session. Their absence cost Yue handling observations the exterior diagram might not reveal.

shoal_e03_private_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_private_03.text: The housing's marked bird looked upside down in her outline. An ordinary supplier hand corrected it from the owner's retained exterior description, and Yue changed the drawing. The private method gave a sharper technical answer to one measured question; it did not make her first sketch accurate. She recorded both the correction and the geometry result. A better tool could narrow uncertainty while leaving a different error exactly where it had been.

shoal_e03_private_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_private_04.text: Before leaving, she separated a public safety warning about a snagging rim from the protected freight-signal appendix. The warning did not disclose the licensed geometry. It could still be issued to affected handlers with the actual observation and scope. Private source terms were no excuse to hide an ordinary hazard. The supervisor approved that distinction and locked the kit in its declared cupboard. Yue kept the custody receipt, not title to the equipment.

shoal_e03_private_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_private_05.text: Rong revised the supplier delivery list using the licensed unloaded result within its stated limits. He could not advertise Yue's body as part of the appendix or imply fueled qualification. The packers received the permitted rim warning later through the public desk, after the private session had ended. Yue had gained a narrow bench answer and lost their presence at the table. That trade remained material even when its safety warning crossed the door properly.

shoal_e03_witness_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_witness_01.text: With the Lark dispatch completed and paid, Yue brought no kit or private appendix to the session. The supervisor used port-owned exterior measuring tools for a bounded ordinary observation, not a substitute private geometry trial. Yan joined as a witness to handling conditions on the safe side of the yard. His current paid crew role gave him no technical source license. He could tell Yue where a line rubbed a housing during ordinary movement.

shoal_e03_witness_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_witness_02.text: Rong wanted the resulting report to answer a supplier fit question. Yue said the permitted exterior observation could not do that. The lost equipment booking was not quietly restored because she had accepted a port job. The supplier would need a separately authorized bench task by someone with the relevant method and tools. Today's useful result concerned contact marks and handling direction. She wrote its limit before anyone could turn the completed dispatch's credibility into a missing instrument.

shoal_e03_witness_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_witness_03.text: Yan showed a scrape made by an ordinary carrying line near the housing's rim. Yue had seen a similar scrape on an exterior lid during her earlier offered observation. Similarity did not identify the same cause. They recorded today's angle, load state, and actual line contact without claiming the earlier mark proved it. Rong looked irritated by the unfinished link, then asked for the current rubbing point to be padded before another ordinary move.

shoal_e03_witness_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_witness_04.text: The padding used the batch's current materials scope and the supervisor's permission. It did not certify the housing's freight-signal geometry or allow fuel. Yue returned the port measuring tools before the shift ended. Her independent report stayed limited to what the witnesses had observed. No lender-owned Lark equipment required a return from this route. A completed carried dispatch and a new accepted shift remained different jobs even when the same clerk filed both pages.

shoal_e03_witness_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_witness_05.text: The supplier list kept the technical fit question pending and incorporated the current handling adjustment separately. Yan went back to his crew's next ordinary task. Yue had gained an independently observed practical change while lacking the private bench result. She could not rank every route by the number of completed boxes on a form. One report helped a handler today; another source might answer a geometry question tomorrow, if its owner actually offered it.

shoal_e03_rejoin_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_rejoin_01.text: On Day Two Hundred Forty, rain drove the sorting into the roofed edge of the yard. Yue shared a bench with the veteran whose handle request had preceded hers. He showed her how a household mark survived beneath a second owner's paint. She asked whether that meant the second sale had been improper. He said it meant paint had not covered a mark. She laughed at the precision and let him finish the story before deciding what it proved.

shoal_e03_rejoin_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_rejoin_02.text: He had once sold a boat to pay a sister's apprenticeship fee. The boat still came through this yard under its later owner's papers. Seeing it hurt, though no one had stolen it. Yue had spent too long expecting every loss to disclose a wrong that could be fixed. The sorter tapped the old mark and said his sister now earned more than he did. He could be proud and miss the boat in the same breath.

shoal_e03_rejoin_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_rejoin_03.text: By Day Two Hundred Forty-Five, Yue had completed ten accepted shifts and received the second twenty-five-copper weekly wage. The first retrieval's surviving materials remained with their owners, and the unchosen crate remained lost. The forty-housing batch moved slowly through unloaded comparison and handling work. Some workers wanted the post to continue past its six-week term. Others worried that another technical appointment would take space from their own craft.

shoal_e03_rejoin_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e03_rejoin_04.text: At the lane, He Ming invited her to hear those disagreements where they began, among workers whose packing tables had been displaced by the proposed restoration layout. Yue agreed to the meeting time rather than volunteering a solution. A yard could still remove someone else's livelihood from its corner.
